messages:
jessica: Heads-up: saw an 8-12ms tail latency bump for small streaming responses on canary after the kernel selection commit yesterday. Repro with short prompts (~30 tokens) and stream=true. dumping traces.
omar: Ugh. Which commit? kernel-selection tweak v2? link to PR
jessica: yeah PR #4123 — it prefers fp16-quant kernels for short sequences. Repro steps:
```
curl -s -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-v1\",\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"stream\":true}' https://canary.redwood/api/v1/stream
```
Observed profiler snippet:
```
host_parse: 0.8ms
grpc_writev: 2.1ms
tokenize: 1.2ms
kernel_launch: 0.5ms
stream_flush: 7.5ms <-- jump
```
liam: stream_flush spikes smell like smallwrite batching. Any change to writev coalescing or grpc framing? could be more DATA frames hitting the wire.
anya: I pushed a tweak to grpc writev batching last month that reduced aggregation for tiny writes. Deploy-bot shows that deploy.
deploy-bot: Deployment event: svc/host-proxy v2.14.0 rolled to canary at 2026-03-19T04:12:21Z
omar: can you grab tcpdump/pcap around the write path? wonder if we're emitting many tiny DATA frames instead of one coalesced write.
jessica: attached pcap: shows ~8 extra DATA frames per short request. KV-cache hit ratio unchanged though.
liam: another angle: kernel selection change might make the RPC return earlier to the user thread (since kernel is faster), which short-circuits batching window. net effect: more flushes. We should look at batching heuristics.
anya: we have flag --stream-smallwrite-delay-ms default 2ms. bumping that might help. try 6ms?
jessica: quick experiment: set to 6ms on canary — p99 dropped ~9ms back to baseline. throughput for large requests dipped.
liam: suggests adaptive delay: longer for stream tiny responses, but short for bulk requests. e.g. delay = clamp(2ms, tokens*0.002ms, 10ms) or per-route config.
omar: also check host KV cache locking: kernel change might shift timing and cause lock contention on lookups, adding host-side latency.
anya: kvcache traces: lookups +0.4ms after kernel switch, mostly lock wait. snippet:
```
[hostkvcache] lookup lock wait: 420us
[hostkvcache] lookup memcopy: 150us
```
neal: fast-path trylock for streaming path? If trylock fails, return cached pointer / miss and continue instead of blocking.
liam: plan: microbench variants: 1) trylock fast-path, 2) current, 3) increased write coalesce. measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput for 32/128/1024 token profiles.
jessica: I'll spin a canary with trylock + adaptive smallwrite delay later today and post numbers.
omar: SGTM. please include perf dashboard links and raw traces. Also mark potential regression window for large-batch throughput.
anya: I'll take ownership of the KV lock patch and benching.
deploy-bot: Canary update: host-proxy v2.14.1 (trylock + adaptive delay) started 2026-03-19T12:03:05Z
jessica: Initial canary numbers: p99 returned to baseline (down ~10ms), p50 unchanged, large-batch 1024-token throughput -1.5%.
liam: OK to merge if e2e and 24h canary look stable. add a rollout plan to revert knob quickly if throughput degrades in prod.
omar: filing follow-up issue #9876 to track: adaptive-delay tuning, kvcache trylock safety, perf dashboards.
jessica: thanks team :thumbsup:
